ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus septentrionalis* reaches 75 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal blotches and possesses a distinct precloacal groove and 18–20 subdigital lamellae under the fourth toe.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus septentrionalis* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of 5–6 distinct, dark, W-shaped transverse bands that are narrower than the interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus septentrionalis* inhabits the moist deciduous forests and rocky foothills of Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus septentrionalis* is a nocturnal gecko that primarily hunts for small invertebrates on rock surfaces and karst formations after dark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus septentrionalis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus septentrionalis* is endemic to the Himalayan foothills in the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, typically occurring at low to moderate elevations.
